basis:
check_commit() declares its arguments as (ROOT, REV) and the `case` dispatcher passed them the other way round, so the documented invocation `--check-commit [REV]` put the revision into the ROOT slot. git -C <not-a-directory> rev-list prints nothing on stdout, the empty rev list was read as 'no commits in HEAD', and the guard exited 0 without looking at a single commit. b126d7d fixed glob_match() -- the engine -- and recorded that check_commit() flagged zero paths across all 11 commits; the wiring was a separate defect and stayed reversed, so the documented command remained fail-open. Three changes, all strengthening, none widening scope: (1) the dispatcher now passes (ROOT, REV) in the order the function declares, ROOT coming from this script's own location as ROOT_DEFAULT always intended; (2) a ROOT that is not a repository and a range git cannot resolve are now exit 2, because the old code could not distinguish 'the range selected nothing' from 'I read nothing at all' and answered both with exit 0; (3) git diff-tree gains --root, without which a repository's first commit is invisible to the check entirely -- live here, where root commit 1f43c9e adds ten R2 paths (three migrations, one rollback, six control-suite files, counted with `git diff-tree --root --no-commit-id --name-only -r 1f43c9e`) and not one was ever reported. Assertions 11a-11d run the script as a SUBPROCESS from inside a fixture repository with ONE argument, because every pre-existing assertion calls guard()/check_commit() directly and therefore cannot see the dispatcher -- that is how this defect survived a fix already reported complete. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are byte-identical to the previous revision: this is a wiring fix, not a scope change. No change to scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh or scripts/run-db-tests.mjs. No migration, no engine change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged. This claim carries no Reviewed-by trailer: the commit is UNREVIEWED and is raised to MediaTech (CTO) for review. There is no independent security reviewer on this team -- that seat was declined by the board on cost -- so a CTO self-review is a recorded degradation, not independent review.

SECOND COMMIT ON THIS ISSUE, from the CTO review of f64cc7d (AFC-220, verdict CHANGES REQUESTED). The reviewer's structural point was that 11a-11d drive the CLI and therefore still could not see a caller one layer further out: f64cc7d shipped with 27/27 green while its only production caller, .github/workflows/ci.yml, passed two arguments (`--check-commit "$PWD" "$range"`) and so exited 2 without reading a commit. The defect class was not closed, it was moved up one layer. This commit closes that layer and nothing else: (a) CHECK_COMMIT_MAX_ARGS=1, declared at the top of the file rather than beside the dispatcher because --self-test runs before the dispatcher is reached; (b) audit_callers(), which walks every tracked file and fails if any shell command invokes the guard with more arguments than the dispatcher accepts, counting arguments quote-aware and stopping at the first unquoted shell metacharacter or a `#` comment; (c) assertions 11e (audits the REAL repository, not a fixture -- auditing a fixture would audit the fixture and always pass), 11f (a planted two-argument caller must be named, so a blinded matcher cannot pass by matching nothing) and 11g (prose that merely mentions the flag must not be flagged, and the one genuine one-argument caller in the probe must still be counted, so a matcher cannot pass by being too loose). A caller that hides the script behind a variable, a wrapper or eval is NOT covered, and the assertion says so rather than implying it is. Also in passing: the unreachable duplicate `return $rc` introduced by f64cc7d is removed, and the 4/1/5 split quoted above is corrected to 3/1/6. GUARDED_PATHS and REVIEW_REQUIRED_PATHS are byte-identical to f64cc7d. No change to scripts/retention-literal-gate.sh or scripts/run-db-tests.mjs, no migration, no engine change, no personal data, so the CTO migration-approval path is not engaged. Again no Reviewed-by trailer: UNREVIEWED, and raised to MediaTech (CTO) on AFC-212.
